doc.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Working with stars and Frank Sinatra in Las Vegas
summary: Pete says stars are generous and tells of flying to Las Vegas for Sinatra and the gun incident.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Judy Garland, Ella Fitzgerald, Peggy Lee, wow. How long do we have here, right? But now—
Just let me, I’m talking too much.
No, what kind of things stick out in your mind with some of these stars? Are they great to work with the majority of them?

Yeah, yeah they are. Usually the more they’ve done, the less frightened they are, and the nicer they are you see? And Frank Sinatra, I played trumpet with Frank for about four or five years. And Frank’s pilots flew me into Vegas many times, at least six or seven times I can think of, because of the one show at ten o’clock, and I finished “The Carol Burnett Show” like about eight thirty or quarter of nine or nine o’clock and I’d try to rush out, they’d have a car for me, and go to Burbank, and they’d take off and I’d be there for the downbeat.
And always, Frank was really great. I was there when the guy pulled the gun on him. There was a big scene that happened. We were all sitting around—

Well somebody had pulled a gun on him, had a gripe for one of the other owners of the places or something, when he drove a golf cart into the pool years before or something. And everybody was sitting there and this older guys comes and says, “How dare you, who do you think you—” and he pulled out a gun and the officers were right there around Frank you know, like it happened like this. And he said, “Okay fellas, that’s it, it’s a wrap.” He had one more show, that’s when we’d do two shows a night at Caesar’s. He said, “It’s a wrap, let’s go.” That was it. We had about another week and a half I think. Oh many incidents happened but I’m sure you’re more interested in the music aspect or how the lives, the things that musicians go through, it can be so difficult you know.
